units.source_text: 却说那常陆介想是身体衰老之故，此时正疾病缠绵。

en.t: Now the Hitachi Assistant Governor, perhaps because his body had grown old and weak, was at this time lingering in illness.

units.source_text: 自知性命垂危，挂念这年轻的妻子，时常向几个儿子谆谆嘱咐：“我死之后，万事由她自己做主。

en.t: Knowing that his life was in grave danger, and anxious for his young wife, he often earnestly instructed his sons, saying, "After I die, let her decide everything for herself.

units.source_text: 你等必须处处照顾她，同我生前一样。”

en.t: You must look after her in every way, just as you did while I was alive."

units.source_text: 朝朝夜夜反复说这几句话。

en.t: Morning and night he repeated these same few words again and again.

units.source_text: 空蝉想起自身本已命苦，今若丧夫，此后孤苦伶仃，生涯何等凄凉！

en.t: Utsusemi thought that her fate had already been bitter, and that if she now lost her husband, she would be left lonely and helpless, with a life of unbearable desolation ahead.
Because of this, she grieved and sighed day and night.
Seeing this, the Hitachi Assistant Governor was deeply saddened.

units.source_text: 但人生寿命有限，留恋亦是徒然。

en.t: But a human life has its limit, and even clinging to it is in vain.

units.source_text: 他担心身后之事，常作可悲的妄想：“我的儿子心地究竟如何，不得而知。

en.t: Worried about what would happen after his death, he often fell into pitiful fancies: "I cannot truly know what is in my sons' hearts.

units.source_text: 为了照顾此人，我总得设法把灵魂留在这世间才好。”

en.t: For the sake of watching over this woman, I must somehow find a way to keep my soul in this world."

units.source_text: 他心中如此想，口上也说了出来。

en.t: What he thought in his heart, he also spoke aloud.

units.source_text: 然而大限到时，无法挽留，终于一命呜呼了。

en.t: Yet when his appointed end arrived, there was no holding him back, and at last he breathed his last.
